instruction: Use Abaqus via the Command Line Interface (CLI) to perform a thermal stress analysis. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Part: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a 10 mm x 10 mm rectangle in the Y-Z plane (Y from 0 to 10, Z from 0 to 10). Extrude along the global X-axis to a length of 100 mm. Property: Create a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3, and thermal expansion coefficient = 1.2e-5 /K. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the bar. Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-ThermalStress. Load: Apply a predefined temperature field of 20 degC to the whole model in the Initial step. Fix both end faces with U1 = U2 = U3 = 0: the left end face at X = 0 and the right end face at X = 100 mm. In Step-ThermalStress, apply a predefined temperature field of 120 degC to the whole model. Mesh: Apply a global seed size of 5 mm. Assign element type C3D8R and generate the mesh. Job: Create a job named Job-ThermalStress, submit it for analysis, and wait for successful completion. Save: Save the model database to C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-ThermalStress.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-ThermalStress.odb. [Software] To start Abaqus/CAE, run `C:\SIMULIA\EstProducts\2023\win_b64\resources\install\cmdDirFeature\launcher.bat cae` (adjust path to your install).
